'''Sir William Davidson Niven''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|KCB|FRS}} (24 March 1842 – 29 May 1917) was a Scottish [[mathematician]] and [[electrical engineering|electrical engineer]].

After an early teaching career at [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge]], Niven was Director of Studies at the [[Royal Naval College, Greenwich]], for thirty years.

==Life==
[[File:Naval College.JPG|thumb|left|200px|Royal Naval College, Greenwich]]
Niven was born at [[Peterhead]] in [[Aberdeenshire]], one of five notable mathematician brothers: [[Charles Niven|Charles]] and James the best known. He graduated first from the [[University of Aberdeen]],<ref name=whitehead>Ronny Desmet, Michel Weber, ''Whitehead. The Algebra of Metaphysics'' (2010), p. 116</ref> then from [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], where he was 3rd [[Wrangler (University of Cambridge)|wrangler]] in 1866.<ref>{{MacTutor|id=Niven}}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of his college.

In 1882 Niven became Director of Studies at the [[Royal Naval College, Greenwich|Royal Naval College]], [[Greenwich]], succeeding [[Thomas Archer Hirst]].<ref name=who>'NIVEN, Sir William Davidson', in ''[[Who's Who (UK)|Who Was Who 1916–1928]]'' (London: A. & C. Black, 1992 reprint, {{isbn|0-7136-3143-0}})</ref> He was appointed a [[Companion of the Order of the Bath]] (Civil division) in [[Queen Victoria]]'s [[1897 Diamond Jubilee Honours|Diamond Jubilee Honours]] of 1897. He retired in 1903, when he was [[knight]]ed by being appointed a [[Knight Commander of the Order of the Bath]].<ref name=who/>

Niven was a colleague of [[James Clerk Maxwell]] (1831–1879), whose scientific papers he edited after his death. Among Niven's students was [[Alfred North Whitehead]], to whom he taught mathematics, by instructing him in the physics of Maxwell.<ref>Frank Northen Magill, Alison Aves (1999) ''Dictionary of World Biography'', p. 3,965</ref>

In retirement Niven lived at Eastburn, [[Sidcup]], [[Kent]],<ref name=who/> where he died in 1917.<ref name=whitehead/>

==Major publications==
Niven edited works by J. C. Maxwell:
* 1881: [[A Treatise on Electricity and Magnetism]], 2nd edition
* 1890: [https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/bibliography/19718#/summary The Scientific Papers of James Clerk Maxwell] from [[Biodiversity Heritage Library]]
